_about: W6 of .build/analysis/seat-model-plan.md — the 2028 candidate set the simulation layer draws around. Per seat: incumbent (who sits now, +recontests: true, false, or null where a member who changed party has not said), member2025 (who the 2025 election returned), the 2028 contest set (groups booleans, coalition party mix, named independent entrants), and basis2025 — the measured 2025 contest set from the DoP — so every 2028 assumption sits next to its fact. contest.on true-but-basis2025.on false marks the ON-everywhere extension (2025: ON skipped only the three ACT seats). Produced by build-candidate-set.mjs from the HAND overlay candidate-overlay-2028.json; test-candidate-set.mjs pins the merge against the W2/W3 data.

assumptions._note: 2025 base, measured in HouseDopByDivisionDownload-31496: ALP and GRN contested all 150; ON contested 147 (absent Bean/Canberra/Fenner — the ACT seats); exactly one Coalition party per seat except the seven LP+NP three-cornered contests (Barker, Bendigo, Bullwinkel, Durack, Forrest, Grey, O'Connor). ON 'everywhere' for 2028 extends past the 2025 base — those seats are flagged in the build output.

incumbent.name: David Farley
incumbent.note: Sussan Ley resigned from Parliament on 27 February 2026; David Farley won the by-election of 9 May 2026 for One Nation (map/data/data-now.json holds the count).

incumbent.name: Barnaby Joyce
incumbent.note: left the Nationals on 27 November 2025 and joined One Nation on 8 December 2025 (map/data/data-now.json). Joyce said in October 2025 that New England would not be recontested, and has since left that open (ABC News, 20 February 2026); recontests stays null until Joyce or One Nation says: the Nationals lose their sitting member either way, and no One Nation member is assumed on the ballot.

incumbent.name: Michelle Landry
incumbent.retirementNote: 2026-10-23 — will not contest the next election (announced 23 October 2026: ABC News, abc.net.au/news/2026-10-23/michelle-landry-capricornia-retirement/107300492). The Nationals' leader, Senator Matt Canavan, has since announced a run for the seat; no candidate is assumed.
